recrosses her legs.

eight, I called his office. He answered, saying that he wouldn't be back until 
late, but I could hear a woman giggling in the background. When I asked him who 
it was, he said that there was nobody else there. But I'm sure that I heard 
someone. That night, after he went to sleep, I checked his clothes and I 
smelled a perfume that I don't wear and saw a smudge of lipstick on his shirt." 
Tears well up in her eyes again, but she keeps talking.

"I just found out that my husband is having an affair," Sandra says. "Well, I 
don't have proof, but I'm almost certain. You see, he's always working late. At 
first, I thought it was just the demanding nature of his work -- he's a manager 
at Logitek -- but later I began to suspect something." She uncrosses and then 
recrosses her legs.

eight, I called his office. He answered, saying that he wouldn't be back until 
late, but I could hear a woman giggling in the background. When I asked him who 
it was, he said that there was nobody else there. But I'm sure that I heard 
someone. That night, after he went to sleep, I checked his clothes and I 
smelled a perfume that I don't wear and saw a smudge of lipstick on his shirt." 
Tears well up in her eyes again, but she keeps talking.

"I have to know for sure, so that I can confront him and deal with the 
situation. I'll pay you well -- $1000 for solid evidence one way or another."

events.intent: Ask calmed client about her husband problem
events.response:
"I just found out that my husband is having an affair," Sandra says. "Well, I 
don't have proof, but I'm almost certain. You see, he's always working late. At 
first, I thought it was just the demanding nature of his work -- he's a manager 
at Logitek -- but later I began to suspect something." She uncrosses and then 
recrosses her legs.

"One night," she continues, "I'd planned a nice dinner. When he wasn't home by 
eight, I called his office. He answered, saying that he wouldn't be back until 
late, but I could hear a woman giggling in the background. When I asked him who 
it was, he said that there was nobody else there. But I'm sure that I heard 
someone. That night, after he went to sleep, I checked his clothes and I 
smelled a perfume that I don't wear and saw a smudge of lipstick on his shirt." 
Tears well up in her eyes again, but she keeps talking.

"I have to know for sure, so that I can confront him and deal with the 
situation. I'll pay you well -- $1000 for solid evidence one way or another."

"Will you help me?" she asks with a pleading look in her eyes.
